traps: Claiming the printing press only affected elite scholars and did not broaden participation.
Stating that the printing press invented the internet or modern digital media.
Providing a vague statement like "it made information spread faster" without linking to who could argue.
Mentioning only the aesthetic change of books without discussing accessibility or literacy.
Suggesting the press reduced censorship as the primary reason for broader participation.

checks.ask: Does the answer give at least one correct reason why the invention of the printing press changed who could take part in public argument?
Does the answer give at least two distinct correct reasons why the invention of the printing press changed who could take part in public argument?
Does the answer explain how the given reasons led to a broader range of people being able to participate in public argument?
